item.title: ‘My message twisted’ - Obi denies telling UK-based Nigerians to abandon loved ones
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has denied asking Nigerians living in the United Kingdom to abandon relatives who depend on them for financial support, saying his message about hardship in Nigeria was distorted by political opponents. Obi said he appreciated Nigerians in the diaspora who made sacrifices to support their families at home, stressing that his concern was the country’s dependence on remittances to meet basic needs. In a statement titled “My Message Has Been Twisted”, posted on X on Tuesday, the former Anambra State governor said he never asked Nigerians abroad to stop supporting their loved ones. “I deeply appreciate Nigerians in the diaspora who work tirelessly and make enormous sacrifices to support their families back home,” he said. “Their remittances pay for school fees, hospital bills, rent, and feeding expenses. Their patriotism and sacrifices deserve our profound respect. I never asked them to abandon their loved ones.” Obi said his message was aimed at drawing attention to the economic conditions forcing millions of Nigerians to rely on relatives abroad for their survival. “My concern is that Nigeria should not remain a country where millions depend on relatives abroad for basic survival,” he said. “Our goal must be to build a nation that provides jobs, affordable healthcare, quality education, and economic opportunities for its citizens.” He accused political opponents of misrepresenting his comments, insisting that his position was about addressing the causes of hardship rather than discouraging financial assistance to families. “Political opponents may twist my message, but the truth remains clear: I am not asking Nigerians abroad to abandon their families. I am advocating for a Nigeria that will no longer abandon its own people,” he said. The clarification followed backlash over comments Obi made during a town hall meeting with diaspora supporters in Manchester on Sunday. In a video that went viral, Obi urged Nigerians in the UK to stop giving money to relatives and others at home who asked them for financial assistance, arguing that such support could ease hardship without addressing its underlying causes. “You have people at home in Nigeria today who are begging you for money. Tell them no!” he said. Obi attributed the country’s economic difficulties to poor leadership and urged Nigerians abroad to encourage their relatives and friends at home to vote for leaders who would prioritise productivity and economic opportunities. item.title: Fuel subsidy return could push Naira to N4,000/$ — Oyedele
item.description: Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has warned that a return to petrol subsidy could trigger capital flight, weaken investor confidence and push the naira to between N3,000 and N4,000 to the dollar. Oyedele gave the warning on Monday during a press briefing at the International Monetary Fund and World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand. He said investors had repeatedly questioned whether the Federal Government would abandon its economic reforms ahead of the next election cycle. The minister ruled out reversing the reforms, warning that even a signal that President Bola Tinubu’s administration was considering reinstating petrol subsidy could unsettle financial markets, increase borrowing costs and worsen economic pressures on households. “In all the meetings I have had, I came to a conclusion that the markets, including the domestic market, which you can read from the capital market, and the international market, have largely written off the opposition in Nigeria as being unserious,” he said. Oyedele warned that any indication of a possible return to subsidy would trigger an immediate market reaction. “If, for any reason, the President were to say we are merely considering the return of fuel subsidy, capital would react immediately. “Airfares would struggle, the naira would come under severe pressure, potentially moving towards 3,000, 3,500 or even 4,000. The very fuel people want subsidised would become far more expensive in naira terms,” he stated. The minister added that capital flight could extend beyond foreign investors, as wealthy Nigerians, business owners and middle-class investors might also turn to the dollar as a hedge against uncertainty, further increasing demand for foreign exchange. Oyedele also rejected suggestions that the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited’s temporary reduction in petrol retail margins amounted to a return to subsidy. He explained that the reduction was a commercial decision rather than a payment funded by public resources, arguing that a company’s decision to lower its profit margin to make a product more affordable should not automatically be classified as a subsidy. item.title: National grid crashes 81% to 675MW, as 9 plants go off
item.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja Nigeria’s grid electricity supply crashed by 81.5 per cent to 675 megawatts (MW) at 1pm on Monday from 3,647MW, following a drop in the number of power plants supplying the national grid from 21 to 2. The development prompted electricity distribution companies, including Abuja Electricity Distribution Company (AEDC) and Ikeja Electric, to issue public notices informing customers of supply constraints linked to challenges on the national grid. Data from the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) showed that 21 power plants were supplying electricity to the grid before the incident at noon, when total generation stood at 3,647MW. However, by 1pm, the number of plants on the grid had dropped to 12, while electricity supply plunged to 675MW, representing a loss of 2,972MW within one hour. The plants that went offline included Azura, Egbin, Jebba and Kainji hydroelectric power plants. The sharp decline followed relatively higher supply levels earlier in the day, with the grid recording 4,331MW at 1am and 4,458MW at 6am. Supply subsequently fell to 3,647MW by noon before experiencing the steep drop at 1pm. Electricity supply later recovered to 2,150MW by 5pm, representing an improvement of 1,475MW from the 1pm level, although it remained significantly below the morning peak. In a public notice issued on Monday, AEDC informed customers that electricity supply from the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) had been interrupted due to a grid-related challenge. The company said TCN’s technical team was working to restore grid stability, adding that power supply was gradually being restored to its feeders. “We assure you that efforts are ongoing to restore full supply across our franchise area as soon as the situation permits,” AEDC said, while apologising for the inconvenience caused by the interruption. Similarly, Ikeja Electric attributed reduced electricity supply across its network to a shortfall in the volume of power allocated to it from the national grid. In its notice to customers, the distribution company said it was engaging relevant stakeholders to improve available supply. It added that it would continue to distribute the electricity received from the grid as efficiently and equitably as possible. However, NISO said it had stabilised the national grid following multiple trippings on the 330-kilovolt (kV) transmission network. In a statement on Monday, the system operator said the incident occurred at approximately 12:40pm on October 19, 2026. It said it immediately implemented corrective measures in collaboration with TCN to stabilise the power system and restore normal operations. According to NISO, restoration efforts had been successfully completed and the national grid had returned to normal operation. The operator clarified that the incident affected only a section of the grid, contrary to unverified reports and claims. item.title: Customs reviews recruitment complaints, screens out 397 applicants
item.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has opened a fresh window for reviewing complaints from applicants disqualified during its recent recruitment exercise, following protests by some shortlisted candidates barred from proceeding to the training college. The Comptroller-General of Customs, Adewale Adeniyi, directed a case-by-case reassessment of the complaints after meeting with some of the aggrieved applicants. The NCS spokesperson, Abdullahi Maiwada, a Deputy Comptroller of Customs, disclosed this in a statement, saying the review was intended to ensure that legitimate grievances received appropriate attention. Adeniyi, however, warned that the exercise would not guarantee automatic admission, stressing that all affected candidates would undergo fresh screening and that anyone found to have engaged in certificate fraud or other criminal conduct would face prosecution. According to Maiwada, the recruitment process involves several stages of verification, including credential and document checks, physical fitness and endurance assessments, medical examinations, age verification and drug screening. He disclosed that 397 applicants were identified with issues relating to substance abuse, physical fitness, medical records, age and submitted documentation, while other candidates were disqualified over irregularities detected during the screening exercise. The spokesperson explained that appearing on the final shortlist did not automatically entitle an applicant to enlistment, as every candidate must satisfy all prescribed requirements before being admitted into the Service. He urged affected candidates who believe they were unfairly disqualified to submit their details and complaints through the designated email address, helpdesk@customs.gov.ng, for consideration. Maiwada advised applicants to provide accurate information to facilitate the examination of their cases, adding that the initiative was designed to address genuine grievances without compromising the integrity of the recruitment process. item.title: NGX Group named Africa’s best Exchange at Euromoney Markets Awards 2026
item.description: By Providence Ayanfeoluwa & Glory Bassey Nigerian Exchange Group Plc (NGX Group) has been named Africa’s Best Exchange at the Euromoney Markets Awards 2026, recognising its contribution to market infrastructure, digital innovation and capital formation. Presented at the Mandarin Oriental Hyde Park, London, on Thursday, 15 October 2026, the award recognises achievements in market development during 2025 and comes amid robust growth in Nigeria’s equities market. A key driver of wider primary-market participation has been NGX Invest, the Group’s electronic public-offering platform, which simplifies subscriptions to public offers and rights issues. The platform played a significant role in Nigeria’s banking sector recapitalisation exercise, facilitating more than N2.8 trillion in capital raising. By September 2026, its distribution network had grown to more than 180 channels spanning stockbrokers, banks and fintechs, with a WhatsApp subscription channel providing investors with an additional channel for subscribing to public offers. Nigeria’s equities market recorded strong growth in 2025, with the NGX All-Share Index gaining 51.19 per cent, equities turnover rising 109.48 per cent to N5.96 trillion and market capitalisation reaching N99.38 trillion. This momentum has continued in 2026. As of 16 October, the All-Share Index had gained 59.07 per cent year-to-date. Equities turnover stood at N7.82 trillion, up 73.78 per cent from N4.50 trillion in the corresponding period of 2025, while market capitalisation reached N160.73 trillion. Temi Popoola, Group Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of NGX Group, said: “This award reflects our continued commitment to strengthening the infrastructure and technology that support capital formation and investment. ‘‘We appreciate the trust and collaboration of our regulators, policymakers, issuers, investors, the stockbroking community and other market participants, whose support contributes to the development of our capital market. ‘‘By widening digital access to investment opportunities, improving market efficiency and deepening connections with other African markets, we are working to make our capital market more accessible, resilient and competitive.” ‘‘We see this not simply as an achievement, but as encouragement to keep building a market that can mobilise capital for businesses and offer broader investment opportunities.” Beyond digital innovation, NGX Group continues to advance sustainable finance through the NGX Net-Zero Programme (N-Zero), implemented in partnership with DEG Impulse gGmbH and Africa Foresight Group, with support through DEG Impulse’s develoPPP programme. The initiative helps Nigerian businesses strengthen climate readiness, establish science-based emissions-reduction targets and develop transition plans that can support access to climate-aligned finance. item.title: ‘APC has more problems within’ - Ndume affirms Shettima’s fear
item.description: Senator Ali Ndume, representing Borno South, has backed Vice President Kashim Shettima’s concern about internal divisions within the All Progressives Congress (APC), saying the ruling party faces more problems within its ranks than from the opposition. Ndume said opposition parties might be resilient and vocal ahead of the 2027 general elections, but argued that the struggle for power and the focus on personalities rather than ideas were more troubling. “I think the Vice President was just blunt. We have more problems within than without because, seeing that the opposition, quite alright, they are both resilient, tough and talking big, but it’s not the major problem,” the senator said. He added that politicians across party lines largely shared similar backgrounds, arguing that their differences were often driven by political platforms and the struggle for power. “That’s why they talk about personality instead of ideas, instead of events or debates on what to do and how to do it, and that’s dangerous,” Ndume said. The lawmaker accused politicians of taking Nigerians for granted, urging greater attention to policy debates and practical solutions to the country’s challenges. Ndume’s remarks followed Shettima’s recent warning that internal divisions within the APC posed a greater concern to the ruling party than its political opponents. The Vice President spoke on Saturday in Abuja at the unveiling of the campaign head office of Arewa for Asiwaju (A4A), a northern coalition supporting the Tinubu-Shettima ticket, where he also inaugurated the group’s campaign structure. “Honestly, I am not afraid of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). I am not afraid of a diminished Peter Obi. But I am more afraid of internal contradictions within our household,” Shettima said. He maintained that unity within the ruling party would be crucial, adding, “If we unite as a people, as a family, we will conquer.” Shettima also warned northern political leaders against supporting Tinubu’s presidential campaign while undermining APC governors contesting at the state level. “There is no point in championing the cause of the presidential election and then undermining the governor in the gubernatorial election. Honestly, it will not go down well with the system,” he said. He urged party members to support APC governors, National Assembly members and Tinubu ahead of the next round of elections. “Let’s rally round our governors. Let’s rally round our members of the National Assembly. Let’s rally round President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and see to the victory in the next round of elections,” the Vice President added. item.title: Eko Power affirms status as Lagos state-licensed electricity distributor
item.description: By Jackson-Kalio Tokoni Eko Power Limited has affirmed its status as the electricity distribution company licensed by the Lagos State Electricity Regulatory Commission (LASERC) to serve the southern parts of Lagos State. The company said its establishment followed changes to Nigeria’s electricity regulatory framework, which devolved regulatory powers over intrastate electricity generation, transmission and distribution to state governments. “Eko Power Limited is the distribution company licensed by the Lagos State Electricity Regulatory Commission (LASERC) to distribute power in the southern parts of Lagos State,” the company said in a statement. It explained that the transition followed the Electricity Act 2023, as amended, and the 2023 constitutional amendment, which empowered state governments to regulate electricity markets within their jurisdictions. The transition was completed in June 2025, when LASERC assumed regulatory responsibility for retail electricity distribution and end-user tariffs in the state, the company added. Explaining its regulatory status, Eko Power said it operates under a distribution licence issued directly by LASERC and is subject to the commission’s tariff methodology and service-level standards. “This is reflected in Eko Power Limited’s own LASERC-approved cost-reflective tariffs and its published service-level commitments across all customer bands and feeders in Lagos State,” it said. “Eko Power Limited exists today because Lagos State exercised its constitutional right to regulate retail electricity distribution within the state,” the company said. “We are licensed by LASERC for distribution and tariffs, and our service commitments to customers are set independently under Lagos State law.” The post Eko Power affirms status as Lagos state-licensed electricity distributor appeared first on Vanguard News .

Parallel-market buying rate: around ₦1,365 per dollar. Parallel-market selling rate: around ₦1,380 per dollar. The parallel-market figures are indicative quotations and may differ among dealers. How much is $100 to naira today? At the indicative rates, $100 is worth approximately ₦133,200 at the official reference rate and ₦138,000 at the parallel-market selling rate. The law exists on paper, but on the ground, it is business as usual. At Calabar’s Watt Market, a trader who gave her name as Iquo laughed off the idea of a ban. “I never hear say government ban this thing,” she said, even as she admitted that enforcement agents had raided her stall a few times. “When they come, I beg them and give them something small, they go release my goods.” Her confession tells its own story: the ban is real, but so is the corruption that quietly kills it. She sells the alcohol in several brands from her stand near the motor park where motorcycle riders pick passengers, and she insisted she had no other business to fall back on. In Ogoja, around the timber market, Egbe Anderson, who openly sells the drinks, asked a reporter a question that stung: “If government is serious, why are supply vans still coming every day from Lagos, Port Harcourt, Aba, and Onitsha? Chief convener of the memorial event, Lady Judith Ojevwe Nwachukwu (nee Deniran) in her welcome address, recalled that the fire incident remained the deadliest single industrial disaster ever recorded in the country, stressing that it was due largely to.alleged corporate negligence and zero maintenance culture of the Federal Government and the operating oil firm. “The community came to national and global consciousness after the tragic October 1998 pipeline explosion that consumed 1,082 lives. That tragedy remains one of the deadliest industrial disasters the world has ever witnessed,” she said. “We note that the Idjerhe pipeline explosion was not an accident; it was an inevitable event owing to corporate negligence and zero maintenance culture of both the Federal Government and the oil multinational companies that laid the pipes. Dr. Mrs. Martha Egbedi, who gave the second lecture, called on the government and other relevant stakeholders to set up an Idjerhe tragedy memorial museum and environmental learning centre where students will come to learn about pipeline safety. She also urged the government and oil companies to conduct a full integrity audit of pipelines running through the Jesse community to avoid another disaster, adding that youths from the area should be employed. “In 1998, we were told it was sabotage. In 2024, the National Oil Spill Detection and Response Agency (NOSDRA) still recorded over 500 spills in the Niger-Delta. When will it end? We demand a full integrity audit of all pipelines in Idjerhe kingdom and a community pipeline surveillance model that employs our own youths, not outsiders. Prevention is cheaper than mass burial,” she said. “Beneath our feet are those buried here from no fault of theirs. If we remember, we must remember correctly. We remember that their families were not compensated. A celebrated environmentalist called it a holocaust. Our people were not criminals. They died because of the failure of the state. Idjerhe women became widows overnight. Our women have carried this pain for 28 years,” she lamented. Gibson Ikanone, who gave the last paper, called for what he termed a diplomatic belligerence approach to get justice for the memories of those consumed in the inferno. He charged the leadership of the Urhobo Progress Union (UPU) to also join the demand for justice for the area. Others who spoke at the event included former member of the House of Representatives representing Ethiope Federal Constituency, Chief Halims Agoda; the lawmaker representing Ethiope West State Constituency in the state House of Assembly, Hon. Achoja Blessing; the Otota of Idjerhe Kingdom, High Chief James Onosia Obriki; and the Unogbrogodo of the kingdom, Chief Solomon Ojaraife, who all lamented the sad incident in their separate speeches. Agoda recalled how he confronted the Head of State, General Abubakar, over the incident when he visited, saying the Head of State, who understood the pain of the community, ordered his soldiers to be civil that day. Agoda echoed the call for justice for the area. He recalled that he was a practising Journalist when the sad incident occurred in 1998, adding that when he rushed to the scene that day, he was overwhelmed by the charred remains of his natives on the ground. “I was a Journalist with a national newspaper when it happened. I was overwhelmed by what I saw when I came to the scene. I had to put myself together before I could do anything,” he recalled. “As a media practitioner, I helped other places in the Niger Delta to fight for justice for their areas . I appeal to you all to help me and my people to fight for justice “ he urged. He also expressed gratitude to the convener of the memorial programme, Lady Judith, and the special guests from the Urhobo Arts Heritage Company Limited led by Professor Godini Godwin Darah, who was represented by the Secretary of the group, Felix Kporhotor. item.description: A wave of drone strikes targeting war-torn Sudan’s army-held capital Khartoum and two western areas controlled by paramilitary forces has killed more than 100 people since Sunday, according to residents, medical workers and paramilitary sources. Residents and medical workers said a drone struck a transport hub where villagers had gathered after a market day to find rides home, killing 80 people. item.title: ‘You Cannot Ask Moses To Go Back To Egypt,’ Tinubu Insists No Fuel Subsidy Return
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has reiterated that there will be no return to the fuel subsidy regime, insisting that his administration took a bold and necessary step to reform the country’s economy. Tinubu spoke on Monday during a meeting with the City Boy Movement, a youth-driven political and advocacy group founded to champion his administration’s agenda. “I came, and I removed the subsidy on my first day. Nigeria would have gone bankrupt; there was nothing left to pay for subsidies,” he said. “I could listen to my political opponents promising a return to subsidy.” Drawing a religious analogy, the president added, “I remember my scripture studies, both in the Bible and the Holy Quran. When Moses (Musa) left Egypt, the Red Sea parted and gave way. You cannot ask Moses to go back to Egypt. With your energy and support, we will never go back to Egypt.” The former Lagos State governor commended the organisation for drumming up support for his administration and urged members to take his government’s achievements to the grassroots. “Those of you who are lucky to work with me have given me all the answers needed and the confidence required to see the coming election as a simple matter,” Tinubu stated. “You will go to your campuses, your markets, and your villages. Make sure every young person you know has a PVC and uses it. Tell them what we have done and tell them what we will do. Campaign with your ideas.” President Tinubu announced an end to fuel subsidy during his inauguration in May 2023. The policy shift sparked an immediate hike in petrol pump prices, rising from under ₦200 per litre to current rates hovering between ₦1,350 and ₦1,405 per litre across major filling stations. While the policy has drawn widespread criticism over the heightened cost of living, the president remains firm on his stance. The federal government maintains that the decision is essential to reset the national economy, reassuring citizens that the initial economic hardship will ease over time.
